source.note: The builder-first program's requirements (BF-*), one acceptance case each, written from the plan's gates BF0 to BF9.

requirements.title: Decisions recorded
requirements.requirement: Record the configuration boundary, the portal access model, the public page model, approvals and business time, money through capabilities, custom entity storage, packs, how an app gives way to a pack, and names, before building.

requirements.title: Register checked
requirements.requirement: Keep the program's requirements in docs/registry/bf.yaml, checked by scripts/registry.py like the platform, Logic and closure programs.

requirements.title: Exact inventory
requirements.requirement: List, file by file, what the apps write for themselves that a gate takes over, from a script anyone can run again.

requirements.title: Closure packages re-scoped
requirements.requirement: Each open closure package a gate takes over, in whole or in part, names that gate.

requirements.title: Portal roles
requirements.requirement: A role marked for the portal holds only own-record rules: no rule for every entity, no delete, cancel, export or import. Portal people hold only portal roles, guests none, and neither is an administrator.

requirements.title: Ownership through links
requirements.requirement: An own-record rule may name a path of at most two links, then optionally a child table, ending at a field holding the person's email. It is enforced when listing, reading, creating, changing and acting, through every interface.

requirements.title: Fields and actions under portal roles
requirements.requirement: A portal person sees no field in a permission group unless a rule grants the group, and runs only the actions their roles allow, under the actions' own conditions.

requirements.title: Generic portal pages
requirements.requirement: The portal shows, from a person's portal roles, their records of each entity, each record, forms to create and change what they may, and the actions they may run, with no app code.

requirements.title: Portal roles administered and previewed
requirements.requirement: Administrators mark a role for the portal, write its rules with their paths, and see what a given portal person would reach and through which rule before giving it.

requirements.title: Proof: two portals as configuration
requirements.requirement: Education's family portal and Healthcare's patient portal, configured as portal roles on the generic pages, reach exactly what the apps' own portal endpoints reach.

requirements.title: Public pages bound to an entity
requirements.requirement: A public page asks the fields chosen for it, checks the answers on the server as a form does, and creates the record through the kernel as the page's own account, with the page's limits.

requirements.title: Availability
requirements.requirement: Free times come from a resource's hours, a length and the records holding it, or from a capacity per date; a time taken between being shown and being booked is refused.

requirements.title: A guest's own link
requirements.requirement: A booking gives its guest a link, kept only as a hash, that expires; through it the guest sees, changes or cancels within the window the page sets.

requirements.title: Mail and limits
requirements.requirement: Confirmation and reminder mails from templates with the record's fields; limits per address and per page; a field only programs fill turns them away.

requirements.title: Proof: booking pages as configuration
requirements.requirement: Healthcare's and Hospitality's booking pages configured as public pages pass the scenarios of the apps' own booking tests.

requirements.title: Approvals on transitions
requirements.requirement: A transition may need approvals: from a role or the person a field names, N of them, each decision kept with who decided, when and on what version.

requirements.title: Independence
requirements.requirement: An approval or transition may bar the record's creator and whoever made a named earlier transition, on every path that makes it.

requirements.title: Delegation and escalation
requirements.requirement: An approver away names who decides for them until a date; an approval not decided within its time goes to a named role and says so.

requirements.title: Targets in business time
requirements.requirement: Business calendars gain hours of the day; a state may have a target in business time, states may pause the clock, and a breach is recorded once.

requirements.title: Proof: approvals as configuration
requirements.requirement: ITSM's change advisory board and incident targets, Hospitality's inspection by someone other than the cleaner, and Government's appeals, configured rather than coded, pass the apps' scenarios.

requirements.title: ERP money and stock steps as capabilities
requirements.requirement: ERP offers, with contracts, effect keys, reversals and refusals: issue a sales or purchase invoice, credit one, take a payment with deductions, post a balanced journal under a cost center, and issue or receive stock.

requirements.title: Driven by decision tables
requirements.requirement: A process or a rule chooses amounts, accounts and items for those steps from a decision table, typed in money.

requirements.title: Proof: money policies as configuration
requirements.requirement: Hospitality's deposit kept on a late cancellation, Healthcare's insurer share and Nonprofit's restricted spending, as processes and tables, leave the books as the apps' tests expect.

requirements.title: Rules without source
requirements.requirement: Derivations and checks are written in typed controls: fields chosen from the record, operators by type, money kept in its currency.

requirements.title: Decision tables without source
requirements.requirement: Decision tables are edited as tables: inputs, outputs, hit policy, ranges, and the gaps and overlaps shown as they are made.

requirements.title: Structured steps without source
requirements.requirement: Each kind of process step has its settings in typed controls: what it calls, its input, its routes, its waits and its people.

requirements.title: Lossless round trip
requirements.requirement: What the controls do not cover stays editable in source and is kept untouched by them; a definition saved from either gives the same digest.

requirements.title: Relative to a record's date
requirements.requirement: A schedule runs a set time before or after a date field of each record, once per record and date; a changed date moves it, a cleared one cancels it.

requirements.title: Repeating schedules
requirements.requirement: A schedule runs every day or week at a time in the workspace's zone, once per occurrence across replicas and restarts.

requirements.title: When a linked document changes
requirements.requirement: A schedule runs when a document a record links to reaches a state (an invoice paid), once.

requirements.title: Mail templates
requirements.requirement: Templates with fields of the record and its links, in the recipient's language where kept, sent through the outbox once per key.

requirements.title: Proof: schedules as configuration
requirements.requirement: Appointment reminders, a record paid when its invoice is settled, and a breach sweep run as schedules without an app's upkeep loop.

requirements.title: Ledger source in Studio
requirements.requirement: Studio reads journal lines by account, account type, cost center, party and date, under the viewer's rights.

requirements.title: Records against the books
requirements.requirement: A report sets records' amounts beside ledger balances per dimension and shows the differences.

requirements.title: Certified metrics on dashboards and objectives
requirements.requirement: A dashboard widget or an objective bound to a certified metric shows its definition's value for the viewer.

requirements.title: Proof: reconciliations as configuration
requirements.requirement: Nonprofit's fund ledger and Property's owner reconciliation as Studio reports give the apps' own figures.

requirements.title: Child tables
requirements.requirement: A custom entity may hold child tables of custom child entities, validated and saved with their parent.

requirements.title: Unique keys
requirements.requirement: A custom entity may declare unique fields and keys of several fields, enforced in the database under concurrency.

requirements.title: Numbering and totals
requirements.requirement: Custom documents take numbering series, and totals over their child rows are computed in exact money.

requirements.title: Links both ways
requirements.requirement: Custom entities link to packaged entities, and packaged entities gain links to custom ones, with titles, merging and erasure as for any link.

requirements.title: Pack format
requirements.requirement: A pack holds entities, fields, workflows, approvals, roles, public pages, rules, processes, schedules, templates, Studio items, seeds and words, in canonical form with a digest and a version.

requirements.title: Signed and installed
requirements.requirement: A pack is signed by its publisher and verified when installed; installing it shows its plan and needs consent to that plan's digest.

requirements.title: Upgraded and removed
requirements.requirement: An upgrade shows what it changes and what of the customer's own changes it affects; removing a pack keeps its records unless the administrator asks otherwise.

requirements.title: Exported between workspaces
requirements.requirement: A workspace's configuration is exported as a pack and installed in another, behaving the same.

requirements.title: Proof: a clinic as configuration
requirements.requirement: A clinic pack built with the gates' features only passes Healthcare's scenarios restated against it.

requirements.title: A small hotel, and what still needs code
requirements.requirement: A small hotel pack passes Hospitality's core scenarios, and what still needed code for either pack is recorded.

acceptance.title: Decisions recorded
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: Record the configuration boundary, the portal access model, the public page model, approvals and business time, money through capabilities, custom entity storage, packs, how an app gives way to a pack, and names, before building.
acceptance.acceptance: docs/builder/decisions.md holds each decision, what it rules out and the gate that carries it out.

acceptance.title: Register checked
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: Keep the program's requirements in docs/registry/bf.yaml, checked by scripts/registry.py like the platform, Logic and closure programs.
acceptance.acceptance: A row claiming a state its evidence does not carry, or a requirement missing from the register, fails the check.

acceptance.title: Exact inventory
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: List, file by file, what the apps write for themselves that a gate takes over, from a script anyone can run again.
acceptance.acceptance: Running scripts/builder_inventory.py over the app repositories at the heads it names writes docs/builder/inventory.md unchanged.

acceptance.title: Closure packages re-scoped
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: Each open closure package a gate takes over, in whole or in part, names that gate.
acceptance.acceptance: The closure register's gates match the plan's section 7, and a gate that does not exist fails the check.

acceptance.title: Portal roles
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: A role marked for the portal holds only own-record rules: no rule for every entity, no delete, cancel, export or import. Portal people hold only portal roles, guests none, and neither is an administrator.
acceptance.acceptance: Each forbidden rule is refused when saved; a member role given to a portal person grants nothing; a portal role grants nothing beyond its own records.

acceptance.title: Ownership through links
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: An own-record rule may name a path of at most two links, then optionally a child table, ending at a field holding the person's email. It is enforced when listing, reading, creating, changing and acting, through every interface.
acceptance.acceptance: A guardian reaches their children's report cards and no one else's; moving a record to another student is refused; the same email in another workspace reaches nothing.

acceptance.title: Fields and actions under portal roles
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: A portal person sees no field in a permission group unless a rule grants the group, and runs only the actions their roles allow, under the actions' own conditions.
acceptance.acceptance: A restricted field appears in no list, record, search or export of theirs; an action outside its condition is refused.

acceptance.title: Generic portal pages
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: The portal shows, from a person's portal roles, their records of each entity, each record, forms to create and change what they may, and the actions they may run, with no app code.
acceptance.acceptance: Walked in a browser signed in as a portal person: lists, a record, a change saved, an action run, and a record of someone else's not reached.

acceptance.title: Portal roles administered and previewed
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: Administrators mark a role for the portal, write its rules with their paths, and see what a given portal person would reach and through which rule before giving it.
acceptance.acceptance: The access explanation names the rule and the path a record was reached through, and why another was not.

acceptance.title: Proof: two portals as configuration
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: Education's family portal and Healthcare's patient portal, configured as portal roles on the generic pages, reach exactly what the apps' own portal endpoints reach.
acceptance.acceptance: The apps' portal assertions pass against the generic interface; deliberate breaks (a path ignored, a group shown, a condition ignored, another workspace reached) fail them.

acceptance.title: Public pages bound to an entity
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: A public page asks the fields chosen for it, checks the answers on the server as a form does, and creates the record through the kernel as the page's own account, with the page's limits.
acceptance.acceptance: An answer outside a field's rules is refused with the field named; the record is created with the page's account as its creator and no other rights.

acceptance.title: Availability
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: Free times come from a resource's hours, a length and the records holding it, or from a capacity per date; a time taken between being shown and being booked is refused.
acceptance.acceptance: Two guests booking the last free time: one succeeds, the other is told it went; times outside hours, on a holiday or in the past are never offered.

acceptance.title: A guest's own link
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: A booking gives its guest a link, kept only as a hash, that expires; through it the guest sees, changes or cancels within the window the page sets.
acceptance.acceptance: A link used after it expires or outside the window is refused; a guessed or altered link reaches nothing; the stored hash cannot be used as a link.

acceptance.title: Mail and limits
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: Confirmation and reminder mails from templates with the record's fields; limits per address and per page; a field only programs fill turns them away.
acceptance.acceptance: The limit stops the next request from one address; the trap field stops a program; the confirmation is queued once per booking.

acceptance.title: Proof: booking pages as configuration
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: Healthcare's and Hospitality's booking pages configured as public pages pass the scenarios of the apps' own booking tests.
acceptance.acceptance: The restated scenarios pass; deliberate breaks (a taken time offered, a link kept in plain, a window ignored, a limit ignored) fail them.

acceptance.title: Approvals on transitions
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: A transition may need approvals: from a role or the person a field names, N of them, each decision kept with who decided, when and on what version.
acceptance.acceptance: With two of three needed, one approval leaves the record where it was, the second moves it, and a decision on a changed record is refused.

acceptance.title: Independence
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: An approval or transition may bar the record's creator and whoever made a named earlier transition, on every path that makes it.
acceptance.acceptance: The person who raised a change and the one who assessed it are both refused as approvers, through the interface, the API and a process.

acceptance.title: Delegation and escalation
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: An approver away names who decides for them until a date; an approval not decided within its time goes to a named role and says so.
acceptance.acceptance: A delegate decides within the dates and not after; an approval past its time appears for the escalation role with the reason.

acceptance.title: Targets in business time
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: Business calendars gain hours of the day; a state may have a target in business time, states may pause the clock, and a breach is recorded once.
acceptance.acceptance: A target of four business hours set on Friday at 16:00 falls due on Monday at 11:00 in a calendar of 9 to 17; time on hold is not counted; a breach is recorded once however often it is swept.

acceptance.title: Proof: approvals as configuration
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: ITSM's change advisory board and incident targets, Hospitality's inspection by someone other than the cleaner, and Government's appeals, configured rather than coded, pass the apps' scenarios.
acceptance.acceptance: The restated scenarios pass; deliberate breaks (one approval counted twice, the creator approving, the clock counting a pause) fail them.

acceptance.title: ERP money and stock steps as capabilities
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: ERP offers, with contracts, effect keys, reversals and refusals: issue a sales or purchase invoice, credit one, take a payment with deductions, post a balanced journal under a cost center, and issue or receive stock.
acceptance.acceptance: Each runs once under one effect key, refuses what its owner refuses, and its reversal leaves the books as they were.

acceptance.title: Driven by decision tables
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: A process or a rule chooses amounts, accounts and items for those steps from a decision table, typed in money.
acceptance.acceptance: A table row decides the amount and account a process step uses, and a gap or overlap in the table is refused before it runs.

acceptance.title: Proof: money policies as configuration
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: Hospitality's deposit kept on a late cancellation, Healthcare's insurer share and Nonprofit's restricted spending, as processes and tables, leave the books as the apps' tests expect.
acceptance.acceptance: The restated scenarios pass with the same ledger lines; deliberate breaks (a share added twice, a window ignored) fail them.

acceptance.title: Rules without source
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: Derivations and checks are written in typed controls: fields chosen from the record, operators by type, money kept in its currency.
acceptance.acceptance: A rule made only in the controls compiles to the same release as its source.

acceptance.title: Decision tables without source
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: Decision tables are edited as tables: inputs, outputs, hit policy, ranges, and the gaps and overlaps shown as they are made.
acceptance.acceptance: A table edited in the controls compiles and shows its gaps and overlaps before it is saved.

acceptance.title: Structured steps without source
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: Each kind of process step has its settings in typed controls: what it calls, its input, its routes, its waits and its people.
acceptance.acceptance: A process made only in the controls runs the same as its source.

acceptance.title: Lossless round trip
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: What the controls do not cover stays editable in source and is kept untouched by them; a definition saved from either gives the same digest.
acceptance.acceptance: Editing in the controls a solution holding an unsupported construct keeps that construct byte for byte.

acceptance.title: Relative to a record's date
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: A schedule runs a set time before or after a date field of each record, once per record and date; a changed date moves it, a cleared one cancels it.
acceptance.acceptance: A reminder 24 hours before an appointment is sent once; moving the appointment moves it; cancelling it sends nothing.

acceptance.title: Repeating schedules
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: A schedule runs every day or week at a time in the workspace's zone, once per occurrence across replicas and restarts.
acceptance.acceptance: Two replicas running the sweep make one run per occurrence.

acceptance.title: When a linked document changes
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: A schedule runs when a document a record links to reaches a state (an invoice paid), once.
acceptance.acceptance: A record linked to an invoice is marked paid once when the invoice is paid, and not on later saves.

acceptance.title: Mail templates
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: Templates with fields of the record and its links, in the recipient's language where kept, sent through the outbox once per key.
acceptance.acceptance: A template naming a field the reader may not see is refused when saved; the mail is queued once per record and occurrence.

acceptance.title: Proof: schedules as configuration
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: Appointment reminders, a record paid when its invoice is settled, and a breach sweep run as schedules without an app's upkeep loop.
acceptance.acceptance: The restated scenarios pass; deliberate breaks (a reminder sent twice, a moved date ignored) fail them.

acceptance.title: Ledger source in Studio
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: Studio reads journal lines by account, account type, cost center, party and date, under the viewer's rights.
acceptance.acceptance: A viewer without rights to the books gets nothing; totals equal the trial balance for the same filters.

acceptance.title: Records against the books
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: A report sets records' amounts beside ledger balances per dimension and shows the differences.
acceptance.acceptance: A journal entry outside the records shows as a difference; matched ones do not.

acceptance.title: Certified metrics on dashboards and objectives
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: A dashboard widget or an objective bound to a certified metric shows its definition's value for the viewer.
acceptance.acceptance: Two viewers with different rights see their own values from one definition.

acceptance.title: Proof: reconciliations as configuration
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: Nonprofit's fund ledger and Property's owner reconciliation as Studio reports give the apps' own figures.
acceptance.acceptance: The reports equal the apps' reports on the same data; a deliberate break (a dimension ignored) differs.

acceptance.title: Child tables
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: A custom entity may hold child tables of custom child entities, validated and saved with their parent.
acceptance.acceptance: Lines saved with a custom document come back in order, with their own rules applied, and go with it.

acceptance.title: Unique keys
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: A custom entity may declare unique fields and keys of several fields, enforced in the database under concurrency.
acceptance.acceptance: Two concurrent saves of the same key: one succeeds, the other is refused naming the field; adding a key over existing duplicates is refused listing them.

acceptance.title: Numbering and totals
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: Custom documents take numbering series, and totals over their child rows are computed in exact money.
acceptance.acceptance: A document's total equals the sum of its lines to the cent; numbers are unique and in sequence per series.

acceptance.title: Links both ways
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: Custom entities link to packaged entities, and packaged entities gain links to custom ones, with titles, merging and erasure as for any link.
acceptance.acceptance: A merged customer moves the custom records linking to it; an erasure reaches personal data in custom records.

acceptance.title: Pack format
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: A pack holds entities, fields, workflows, approvals, roles, public pages, rules, processes, schedules, templates, Studio items, seeds and words, in canonical form with a digest and a version.
acceptance.acceptance: Two packs from the same definition have the same digest; a changed word changes it.

acceptance.title: Signed and installed
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: A pack is signed by its publisher and verified when installed; installing it shows its plan and needs consent to that plan's digest.
acceptance.acceptance: A pack altered after signing, or signed by an unknown key, is refused; a consent to another plan is refused.

acceptance.title: Upgraded and removed
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: An upgrade shows what it changes and what of the customer's own changes it affects; removing a pack keeps its records unless the administrator asks otherwise.
acceptance.acceptance: An upgrade over a customer's change shows it and keeps it; removal leaves the records readable.

acceptance.title: Exported between workspaces
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: A workspace's configuration is exported as a pack and installed in another, behaving the same.
acceptance.acceptance: A pack exported from one workspace and installed in another passes the same scenarios.

acceptance.title: Proof: a clinic as configuration
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: A clinic pack built with the gates' features only passes Healthcare's scenarios restated against it.
acceptance.acceptance: The restated scenarios pass against the installed pack with no app code; deliberate breaks fail them.

acceptance.title: A small hotel, and what still needs code
acceptance.setup: A workspace with ordinary roles and a second workspace where it matters, on the platform at the gate's merge.
acceptance.exercise: A small hotel pack passes Hospitality's core scenarios, and what still needed code for either pack is recorded.
acceptance.acceptance: The restated scenarios pass; the record names each remaining piece of code and why.
